body: Kitchen of Purpose teaches cooking as both a craft and a career. Its students learn real culinary skill, and the program is built to land them in real hospitality jobs across the region.

What makes it a WestXDC story is who's standing behind it. Arlington County funds the work with $75,000. The Jacques Pepin Partnership — the foundation carrying one of cooking's great names — adds $50,000. And Hilton Arlington National Landing partners on the workforce side, so the pipeline ends at an actual employer, not a dead end.

Public investment, foundation support, creative craft, and a business that hires, all in one small Arlington nonprofit. That's the region's currents converging in a single room, and it's exactly the kind of connection this map exists to make visible.
summary: A culinary school in Arlington where county funding, a legendary chef's foundation, and a Hilton hiring partner all meet in one kitchen.
title: The Teaching Kitchen Where Arlington's Currents Meet

body: The most creative address in Northern Virginia food might be an office tower in Rosslyn. Nestlé USA runs its innovation and marketing machinery from its headquarters at 1812 N Moore Street, where roughly 900 to 1,000 people work.

There's Open Channel, the company's own idea-acceleration program — Fast Company named Nestlé USA a Best Workplace for Innovators in 2023, crediting more than 8,000 employee ideas and 37 launched initiatives with products on shelves. There's an R&D Accelerator site with a physical Innovation Kitchen Lab. And there's the Center for Marketing Excellence, steering brands known in every grocery aisle in America.
It's the pattern WestXDC keeps hunting for: creative innovation hiding in an industry nobody thinks to look in, running at scale right here.
summary: A global food company runs its idea accelerator, an R&D kitchen lab, and its marketing center of excellence out of Rosslyn.
title: Inside the Innovation Kitchen at Nestlé's Rosslyn HQ

body: Who funds high school theater in Chantilly? The disposal company does.

Evergreen Disposal Services supports the Chantilly High School Drama Department — a tie our social listening surfaced this week from public posts, the kind of relationship that never appears on a roster or a directory page. A waste-services business quietly bankrolling student actors, stage crews, and set builders.

It's a small tie with a big meaning. A better-connected region is better business for everyone in it, including the folks who'll haul the set away when the run ends. WestXDC maps these connections because they're the stitching that holds a place together.
summary: Evergreen Disposal Services funds the Chantilly High School drama department. Nobody's directory has that tie. Ours does.
title: The Disposal Company That Funds High School Theater

body: Dinner in Clarendon comes with a rotating art show, and the artists are your neighbors.

Westville Clarendon partners with the Arlington Artists Alliance to hang local artists' work in the restaurant — the restaurant announced the partnership on its own channels this summer, general manager on camera, artwork by Bryan Jernigan on the walls. The same spot runs one-night fundraisers for local causes, from recovery programs to high school crew teams.

Hospitality spaces like this are the region's connective tissue. A restaurant doing double duty as a gallery gives artists an audience, gives diners a neighborhood, and gives the map one more tie worth drawing.
summary: A Clarendon restaurant hangs local artists' work on its walls — a neighborhood spot doing double duty as gallery infrastructure.
title: Dinner and a Gallery: Westville Clarendon × Arlington Artists Alliance

body: A community bank's job doesn't end at the loan window.

Burke & Herbert Financial Services partners with the City of Alexandria Workforce Development Center on workforce sessions — the Center announced the work on its own account, which is the kind of corroboration our map trusts most. The bank also gave $5,000 to The Campagna Center, Alexandria's long-running family-services nonprofit.
Finance meeting Workforce, with a public-sector partner in the middle. In a region bracing for workforce change, a bank that teaches job skills alongside lending money is a current worth following.

summary: Burke & Herbert partners with Alexandria's Workforce Development Center and funds The Campagna Center — a bank's community role, on the record.

body: A quarter of a million dollars moved through Northern Virginia's charitable economy this fall, and the announcement lived where announcements live now — in a post.

The Builders FirstSource Foundation gave $250,000 to Blood Cancer United, sharing the news on its own channels in September. Blood Cancer United also runs a program partnership with Subaru of America through Subaru Loves to Care, the automaker's community program.
Neither tie sat on the organization's own pages. Our map found them by listening on the counterparty side — one more reason the graph reads relationships, not just listings.
summary: The Builders FirstSource Foundation gave $250,000 to Blood Cancer United — a gift announced in a donor's post, found by listening on the counterparty side.
title: $250,000 for the Fight Against Blood Cancer

body: A bike shop in Arlington is really a youth-development program with a repair stand.

At Phoenix Bikes, young people learn to build and fix bicycles — hands-on making that teaches mechanical skill, patience, and the feel of finishing something real. The organization partners with the Fairfax-Falls Church Community Services Board, the region's public behavioral-health body, connecting the shop's work to the wider support system around local kids.
Craft, confidence, and a first work skill, delivered one derailleur at a time. That's workforce development you can hold in your hands.
summary: Phoenix Bikes teaches Arlington kids to build bikes — and partners with the region's public behavioral-health board.
title: Wrenches, Confidence, and a First Work Skill

body: Somewhere in Northern Virginia sits the switchboard for a global conversation: how mobile technology can teach the world's kids.

The Mobiles for Education Alliance convenes funders, practitioners, and researchers working on education technology for low-resource settings worldwide. Its record shows support ties to Amazon Web Services and the World Bank, and its convenings pull that global community together in person.
The region's reputation runs on federal work, but plenty of its organizations work on the whole planet's problems. This one's classroom is everywhere.
summary: The mEducation Alliance convenes the world's education-technology funders and practitioners — from right here.
title: The Global Ed-Tech Conversation Runs Through Northern Virginia

body: Here's a partnership nobody predicts: the world's best-known conservation organization and a luxury beauty house, running a program together.

WWF and Dior Beauty's programs partnership surfaced in our social listening this week. Brand craft is a real creative industry — storytelling, design, and audience-building at the highest level — and here it's attached to conservation outcomes, with a global fashion house's marketing engine pointed at the planet's most urgent cause.
Unexpected pairs are kind of our thing. The map keeps finding them because the region keeps making them.
summary: WWF and Dior Beauty run a programs partnership — the pairing nobody predicts, surfaced by social listening.
title: Conservation Science Meets the Beauty Counter

body: The defense economy is supposed to run on procurement. Parts of it run on partnership instead.

SOSi, the Reston-based services firm, evidences an innovation partnership with Janes — the defense-intelligence house whose data the world's militaries and ministries rely on. SOSi also shows up as platinum sponsor of the NOTIS 2026 conference and silver at ATA66, backing the language-services profession that sits at the core of its own work.
Even in GovCon country, the interesting motion is creative collaboration: shared data, shared craft, and a company investing in its professional community's gatherings.
summary: Reston's SOSi partners with Janes on innovation — plus platinum support for its own professional community's conferences.
title: An Innovation Partnership in the Heart of GovCon Country
